subject: RE: Urgent — 5xx/429 spike & retry storm affecting AcmeCorp (exec visibility)
messages:
From: Jessica Liao <jessica.liao@acmecorp.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-17T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: High 5xx/429 spike — customer timeouts (urgent)

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

We started seeing a large spike in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood API around 11:22 PDT. Our front-end is seeing customer-facing timeouts and clients are aggressively retrying which looks like a retry storm — page attached logs. Error rate went from ~0.5% to ~18% within 10 minutes.

Impact: customer sessions fail to complete, important batch jobs are timing out. We saw ~1200 failed requests/minute at peak. Our ops team tried increasing client-side backoff but the issue persists.

We’ve attached a short log dump (acme_error_spike-logs.txt) and a screenshot of our KPIs. Please escalate — we need an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA. If this is on your side, we need a call now.

Thanks,
Jessica
VP Engineering, AcmeCorp

Attachments: acme_error_spike-logs.txt, kpi-snapshots-20260517.png

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Liao <jessica.liao@acmecorp.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-17T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike — customer timeouts (urgent)

Hi Jessica — thank you for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. I’m looping in Sean and Hannah from SRE for immediate triage and Laura/Marissa for exec visibility.

Short plan while we triage:
- We’ll enable a temporary, per-tenant rate limit on Acme to reduce the impact of retry storms (expected within 10–15m).
- Deploy a fallback routing rule to direct Acme traffic to the smaller, more stable model variant (should reduce latency and 5xx).
- Ask you to throttle client retries (increase backoff) — if you can push a short config change that would help immediately.

We’re standing up a 30-min bridge now. Joining: Sean (SRE), Hannah (Networking), me.

Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jessica.liao@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-05-17T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike — initial triage notes

Triage notes (observed at 11:22–11:45 PDT):
- Spike correlates with elevated DNS resolution latency to our inference endpoints located in us-west-2. Route53 health checks show intermittent resolver timeouts.
- Upstream: AWS reported a partial networking degradation in us-west-2 around the same time (https://status.aws.amazon.com/ pending).
- Symptoms: increased TCP connect timeouts at edge, causing our API gateways to cascade 502/504s; client libraries are retrying aggressively, producing 429s from our rate limiter once requests reach our frontends.

Immediate actions taken (11:35–11:46):
- Enabled tenant-specific soft rate limit for Acme to reduce retry flooding (rolled back at 12:40 after stabilization).
- Pinned Acme to a smaller model variant to reduce token generation latency (deployed 11:40).
- Added short-term client-facing header (Retry-After: 5s) via gateway to encourage exponential backoff.
- Increased replicas in the affected us-west-2 pool and forced some routing to us-east-1 where healthy capacity exists.

Next steps:
- Hannah to verify DNS provider (FastDNS) path and coordinate with AWS networking.
- Collect a full packet/log capture and attach to RW-INC-3412.
- Recommend a post-incident runbook update: detect DNS latency >200ms and automatically shift routing.

PagerDuty: https://acmecorp.pagerduty.com/incidents/PDI1234 (incident created 11:32). Logs attached (pd-incident-1234.pdf).

—Sean
SRE Lead

Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike — still seeing retries from clients

Thanks for the fast response and for the mitigation work. We still see high retry volume from mobile clients — many of our customers are seeing degraded UX. FastDNS support confirmed a partial outage on their side between ~11:20–11:50 PDT; they say they’ve routed around the issue but some resolvers will cache the failing TTL for a short while.

Question for Redwood: two asks from our side — 1) can you confirm whether you will provide a credit for the downtime window and 2) can we schedule a post-mortem (we’d like to be included). We need a timeline for permanent mitigation (automatic routing away from affected DNS/region).

—Jessica

Subject: Executive summary: AcmeCorp outage impact and ask (credit + remediation)

Team — short executive summary and recommended asks for AcmeCorp escalation:

Timeline (UTC/PDT):
- 2026-05-17 18:20 UTC (11:20 PDT): DNS resolver latency spike begins; correlates with AWS us-west-2 networking degradation.
- 11:22–11:40 PDT: elevated 5xx/429; peak error rate ~18% for Acme tenant.
- 11:35–11:46 PDT: mitigations applied (tenant rate-limit, fallback model routing, extra replicas, cross-region routing).
- 12:10 PDT: metrics dropped to baseline; tail errors resolved by 12:40 PDT.

Customer impact: ~1,200 failed req/min at peak; short-lived but user-visible degraded sessions across mobile and web; Acme requests replayed by clients amplified the problem.

Root cause (interim): partial DNS/resolution failures plus an AWS networking event in us-west-2 that caused higher connect latencies and cascading gateway timeouts. FastDNS reported a partial outage; we are awaiting their full post-mortem.

Immediate remediation proposed (for approval):
1) Offer Acme a one-time service credit equal to 10% of May month-to-date usage or a 2-week free extension (ops decision).
2) Commit an SRE project to implement automated region failover when DNS/latency thresholds trigger (ETA 6 weeks).
3) Update runbooks to automatically apply tenant-specific soft rate limits and gateway Retry-After headers for detected DNS storms.
4) Schedule joint post-mortem with Acme + FastDNS + Redwood engineering within 72 hours.

Owner recommendations:
- Customer credit & commercial ask: Marissa (Sales lead)
- SRE project: Sean + Hannah
- Postmortem coordination: Rishi (owner) + Acme technical contact Jessica Liao

Please reply with approval for (1) the one-time credit and (2) the 6-week remediation commitment. I will coordinate the customer call and the post-mortem.

Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
